items.title: How many CI runs execute a malicious postinstall script before anyone notices?
items.description: At Northfield Ledger, `case-fold` v2.4.1 sat in the lockfile for 14 days before an unrelated audit caught the outbound network call — and every one of those days, CI kept running fresh installs that re-executed the payload. Drag how many CI jobs run per day and how many days pass before detection to see why the exposure isn't 'one leak' but a growing number of executions, each one an independent chance to exfiltrate something new.

params.name: ciRunsPerDay
params.label: CI jobs that run npm install per day

params.name: daysToDetect
params.label: Days until the compromise is detected

outputs.label: Times the payload executed before detection

items.title: How many transitive dependencies would automatically pick up a malicious version overnight?
items.description: L3's tree walker flags any dependency with a caret or tilde range as able to drift to a new version with zero code review. Northfield's real tree had a small handful of transitive dependencies, most left at their default loose ranges (`^`) because nobody had reason to think about them. Drag the total number of transitive dependencies and the share left at loose ranges to see how many packages could silently update to a compromised version on the very next install, with no diff for anyone to catch.

params.name: transitiveDeps
params.label: Total transitive dependencies in the tree

params.name: loosePercent
params.label: Percent left at a loose (^/~) range

outputs.label: Dependencies that could silently drift to a new version
